notes: The it of Let it not be known is kept with the impersonal verb whose person and number it realizes; rule 44's boundary sentence limits rule 20's added-it ruling to a verbless clause, and here a verb stands to be recast. Reading it as an anticipatory expletive was the competing analysis.
before fuses the preposition with the adverb, headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme (rules 30, 23).
one ... another renders the reciprocal idiom, the possessive suffix going unrendered.
Both underdetermined ketiv/qere units resolve to the base reading and change nothing here (rule 9).
